record.title: Guidance-TTT trains a compact strategic guide while keeping the solution executor frozen
record.summary: A 5 October 2026 preprint proposes Guidance-TTT, which updates a compact 8B or 14B model to suggest high-level changes while a stronger GLM-5.2 executor remains frozen and implements each proposal as a complete candidate. An executable verifier scores candidates; an archive and PUCT selection supply parents for later attempts. Authors report results on Polyomino Packing, Lasso path optimization, AHC058 and TriMul, including 91.89 on Polyomino, 0.1739 on Lasso, an AHC058 score of 850,082,731, and 1,129 μs TriMul latency. These are author-reported outcomes against heterogeneous prior references, not matched replications. Key model-scale comparisons use one trajectory, implementation failures affect verifier rewards, and full code/data artifacts have not been independently audited here.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Guidance-TTT updates a compact guidance model that proposes parent-conditioned strategic edits while a stronger GLM-5.2 executor remains frozen and implements complete candidate solutions.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Authors report results on Polyomino Packing (91.89), Lasso (0.1739), AHC058 (850,082,731) and TriMul (1,129 μs), with heterogeneous task-specific baselines.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: A separate Polyomino configuration reports about 58% lower service cost when adapting 8B guidance rather than a 120B model, with scores 83.19 and 83.72; this does not establish general cost reduction.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Single trajectories, differing protocols and candidate implementation failures limit conclusions about general search productivity and cost.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent multi-seed reproduction under matched guidance controls and equal total candidate/API/GPU budget.
Full external run archives and hash-bound payloads were not fetched or verified, and full cost accounting against all baselines is incomplete.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported gains and reduced adaptation cost survive matched independent replication, training a compact model to propose strategic changes while a stronger executor remains fixed could improve the economics of verifier-guided search across coding and scientific optimization. Current evidence is one author-run preprint with heterogeneous baselines, limited repeated trials and execution failures that confound reward; consequence is major but conditional.
limitations: Baseline protocols, candidate budgets, hardware, and score aggregation differ across tasks; headline comparisons are not uniformly matched.
AHC058 reports a single official submission score rather than repeated-run means; TriMul timing is configuration-specific and compares selected eligible Triton entries.
Key model-scale comparisons have one trajectory, leaving search randomness as an alternative explanation.
Verifier reward combines strategic proposal quality with executor implementation validity; invalid candidates can receive zero reward even when the guidance idea is useful.
A separate 58% service-cost result compares one Polyomino configuration and does not establish general economics.
No independent reproduction was performed; linked GitHub run-manifest retrieval failed in this bounded review, and external hash-bound payloads remain unaudited.

An executable verifier scores candidates; an archive and PUCT selection supply parents for later attempts. Authors report results on Polyomino Packing, Lasso path optimization, AHC058 and TriMul, including 91.89 on Polyomino, 0.1739 on Lasso, an AHC058 score of 850,082,731, and 1,129 μs TriMul latency. These are author-reported outcomes against heterogeneous prior references, not matched replications. Key model-scale comparisons use one trajectory, implementation failures affect verifier rewards, and full code/data artifacts have not been independently audited here.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report stronger results than selected prior references across four tasks and a configuration-specific reduction in service cost when adapting an 8B guide rather than a 120B solution model. The cost comparison is one Polyomino configuration and does not establish general compute economics.
technical.compute_or_cost: One separate Polyomino comparison reports about 58% lower service cost for adapting 8B guidance with GPT-OSS-120B execution than adapting the 120B model, at scores 83.19 and 83.72; this is configuration-specific. Attempt counts and full candidate/API/GPU budgets are not consistently matched to all baselines.
technical.demonstrated_result: The authors report 91.89 on Polyomino Packing, 0.1739 on Lasso, 850,082,731 on an AHC058 submission and 1,129 μs geometric-mean latency on TriMul. Main runs use 30 updates, 8 parent groups and 16 rollouts per group. Baselines vary by task and are often prior-work results rather than matched same-budget runs.
technical.implementation_status: Preprint links a public project/implementation; this activation did not fetch the full run manifest, execute code or independently verify remote artifact hashes.
technical.mechanism: A compact guidance model receives a selected parent solution, its summaries and verifier score, proposes a high-level natural-language change, and a frozen stronger executor implements that change into a full candidate. An executable verifier scores the candidate; a parent-linked archive and PUCT selection guide later attempts. Only the compact guidance policy is updated from grouped verifier feedback.
technical.novelty: Apply test-time RL to high-level parent-conditioned strategic edits while a stronger frozen model implements full solutions, separating guidance learning from code-generation adaptation.
technical.regime: Offline verifier-guided search without web access on Polyomino packing, Lasso path optimization, AHC058 production planning and TriMul GPU-kernel optimization. Qwen3-8B or Qwen3-14B guidance is adapted while GLM-5.2 remains frozen. Several headline references are not same-budget or repeated-seed comparisons.
technical.reproducibility: The paper reports setup and ablations, but there is one trajectory for key model-scale comparisons, full external payloads were not recovered, and no independent reproduction was performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: Task-specific published references including CORAL, TTT-Discover, OpenEvolve, SimpleTES and public eligible Triton leaderboard entries. Their protocols, budgets, hardware and result aggregation are heterogeneous; matched frozen-guidance ablations on Polyomino and TriMul are the most relevant internal controls.

brief.title: Guidance-TTT trains a compact strategic guide while keeping the solution executor frozen
brief.why_it_matters: Separating strategic proposals from full solution implementation could reduce the cost and credit-assignment burden of test-time search: a small model learns which change to try while a stronger fixed model handles implementation. The reported results span four coding/scientific optimization tasks, but mixed baselines, single-trajectory scaling results and invalid executable candidates leave the generality and economics unresolved.
